caseno: Appeal from Original Decree No. 34 of 1991.
lawyer:
Akram Hossain Amin, Advocate ------ For the Appellant.

Moktar Hossain ------ Appellant 
VS
Budhi Bala Dashi ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
7. Mr. Akram Hossain Amin, the learned Advocate appearing for the defendants-appellants, submits that the application for letters of administration itself is not maintainable inasmuch as it appears from the Will that the petitioner-respondent No. 1 was only given 14 bighas of land under the Will but she filed the suit for granting the letters of administration with regard to all the properties of the Will, which is illegal. To fortify his submission he refers to AIR 1925 Lahore 493 and relies on it. The second submission of Mr. Akram Hossain Amin is also on maintainability of the suit and he submits that the suit was not maintainable at all inasmuch as there was no estate left whatever to be administered as the suit property had already been sold by the real owners to the defendants-appellants through registered sale deeds of different dates and they are in possession of the same as purchasers. For this submission he relies on the decision reported in 14 CWN 463. The submission of Mr. Amin is that inordinate delay in applying for letters of administration after withdrawing an earlier application raises suspicion about the genuineness of the Will and this aspect was not considered by the trial Court. On this point Mr. Amin refers to the decision of the Appellate Division reported in BSCR Vol. 7 at page 1. The further submission of Mr. Akram Hossain Amin is that the suit is barred by limitation and the learned Court below illegally decreed the still-born suit. For this submission the learned Advocate of the appellants relies on a decision reported in AIR 1987 P & H at page 122. The final submission of Mr. Amin is that in the schedule of the plaint properties have been described beyond the schedule of the Will and the learned trial Court did not notice that and granted letters of administration with regard to the properties described in the schedule of the plaint which is illegal and beyond jurisdiction. 

 9. The first submission of Mr. Akram Hossain Amin is absolutely misconceived and erroneous. There is no provision or restriction in the Succession Act that legatee cannot apply for granting letters of administration with regard to all the properties of the Will if there is no executor. Rather, the legal position is that in the absence of an executor/executrix a legatee is entitled to apply for the grant of letters of administration of the properties bequeathed through the Will. The case cited and relied on by Mr. Amin is of no help to him. It does not support the proposition put forward by him. The decision is other way round. There the issue was whether the petitioner could apply for grant of letters of administration in respect of the part of the property of the deceased covered by the Will and it was argued that the application was not in proper form inasmuch as an inventory of the entire property covered by the Will was not annexed to the application. The application related to only one particular item which was bequeathed to the petitioner. The contention put forward before the Court was that Letters of Administration cannot be granted in respect of part of the property covered by the Will. The Court rejected the contention on the ground that there is no provision in the Succession Act prohibiting the grant of letters of administration for part of the property only. The contention of Mr. Amin that the plaintiff-respondent is not entitled to apply for letters of administration of all the properties of the Will is not tenable in law. Since the executrixes are dead and the plaintiff is the only surviving legatee under the Will she is entitled to apply for the grant of letters of administration of the Will. The second point urged by Mr. Amin is that the learned trial Court ought to have dismissed the suit on the ground that no estate was left to be administered as the appellants had already purchased the suit lands from the lawful owner Jitendra and Achinta. On this point Mr. Amin relies on a decision reported in 14 CWN 463. There the owner of the property died intestate and after his death the property left by him was inherited by his surviving wife. After the death of the wife an application for granting letters of administration was filed to grant letters of administration to the estate of Harish Chandra, the original owner. It was argued in that case that the estate of Harish Chandra was fully administered during the long life-interest of his widow, that there is no necessity to grant letters of administration to anyone for any purpose. The Court taking into consideration the fact that no administration was ever granted during the long series of years during which the widow was in possession of the estate of Harish and when the debts, if any, must have been paid up and all other necessary actions had been taken in connection with the administration of that estate, held that the application was incompetent. In that case the deceased died intestate and there was no Will and the property devolved on the heirs. The Court allowed the appeal on the ground that the real object of the case was not to administer the estate of Harish but to obtain a declaration for heirship so as to fortify the successful party in a regular suit that may thereafter be instituted. The said case has no manner of application in the instant case. We do not, therefore, find any substance in this submission of Mr. Amin. His third submission was on the delay in applying for grant of letters of administration and he relied on the decision reported in BSCR Vol. 7 at page 1. The case does not help him, rather it goes against him. It has been held in this case that where execution and attestation of the Will are proved suspicion caused by unusual delay in applying for probate is negated. In the instant case the execution and attestation of the Will has been duly proved and the Will has been marked as Ext. 1. Mr. Amin also states that he has no grievance against the Will and he admits that the Will is genuine one. Accordingly, we do not find any substance in the contention raised by the learned counsel for the defendant appellants. The 4th submission of Mr. Amin is that the application for grant of letters of administration is barred by limitation inasmuch as the testator died on 6th April. 1936 and the suit was filed on 18.8.76 long after the period of limitation. In this respect he relies on a decision reported in AIR 1987 P & H 122. Before we take up this point for consideration it may be stated that in India Law of Limitation has undergone a change and a new Limitation Act has been enacted in 1963. Under the new law one has to apply for granting of probate or letters of administration within three years from the date of knowledge in view of the changed definition of the words applicant and application contained in section 2 (a) and 2 (5) of the Limitation Act, 1963. But in our country an application for probate or letters of administration is governed by the old law i.e. the Limitation Act, 1908 and there is no bar of limitation in applying for the grant of probate or letters of administration or revocation thereof , The law is well settled on this point and the decisions reported in AIR 1937 Cal 595; AIR 1924 (Mad.) 578; AIR 1931 Cal 717; AIR 1916 Cal 938; AIR 1959 Cal 8 & 81 and AIR 1949 Nag 154 still govern the field . The decision relied on by Mr. Amin is irrelevant and not attracted in the instant case. This submission is also devoid of any substance. The final submission of Mr. Amin is not borne out by the materials on record. We have perused the exhibited documents but do not find any thing in them in support of his contention. Moreover, the decree is very clear and there is nothing ambiguous in it. There is no scope of issuing a letter of administration beyond the schedule of the Will. We are, therefore, unable to accept this submission also.
